title: Microsoft SQL Server Small Examples
description: Use these small Microsoft SQL Server examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Calculate a named answer
examples.description: T-SQL SELECT can return a calculation. AS gives the output column a name that explains the answer.
examples.output: The query returns total_books equal to 7.

examples.title: Keep a local variable
examples.description: A T-SQL variable starts with @. DECLARE gives it a type and an optional starting value.
examples.code:
DECLARE @name nvarchar(40)=N'Mia';
SELECT N'Hello, '+@name AS greeting;
examples.output: The result is Hello, Mia. N marks a Unicode string literal.

examples.title: Make a table variable
examples.description: A table variable holds a small set of rows inside a batch.
examples.output: The two titles appear in id order.

examples.title: Choose top rows with a clear order
examples.description: TOP limits the returned rows. ORDER BY tells SQL Server which rows count as first.
examples.output: Tiny Seed is returned because it has fewer pages.

examples.title: Filter rows with two rules
examples.description: WHERE can combine tests with AND. A row must pass both tests to be included.
examples.output: Only Moon Trip passes both rules.

examples.title: Summarise groups
examples.description: GROUP BY collects rows with the same category.
examples.output: Blue totals 5 books, and Green totals 4.

examples.title: Read related tables
examples.description: A join matches rows by keys. The relationship should be explicit instead of relying on row order.
examples.output: The result joins Moon Trip with author Mia.

examples.title: Handle a conversion that may fail
examples.description: TRY_CAST attempts a type conversion. It returns NULL when an ordinary conversion fails, so code can handle the missing result.
examples.code:
SELECT TRY_CAST(N'12' AS int) AS good_value,
       TRY_CAST(N'twelve' AS int) AS missing_value;
examples.output: The first value is 12 and the second is NULL.

examples.title: Number a sorted result
examples.description: ROW_NUMBER assigns a sequence based on its window order.
examples.output: Tiny Seed is numbered 1, and Moon Trip is numbered 2.

examples.title: Undo a sample transaction
examples.description: A transaction can keep related changes together.
examples.output: The temporary table remains, but rows_left is 0 because the insert was rolled back.

examples.title: Pass a query parameter
examples.description: A parameter keeps a data value separate from the SQL command text.
examples.output: The parameter value 4 produces next_number equal to 5.

examples.title: Let an identity column make an id
examples.description: An IDENTITY column generates numeric values for new rows.
examples.output: The inserted sample row is returned with its generated id and title.
